era_context: 2026 sits in a period of intensifying great-power competition, wide deployment of generative AI and routinised climate-driven disasters. The war in Ukraine enters its fifth year, the Middle East is still realigning after the conflicts that followed 2023, and the United States marks its 250th anniversary while holding midterm elections under rising protectionism and technology controls. Entries for this year cover only scheduled or constitutionally fixed events; no results are recorded.
geographic_coverage_gaps: Domestic politics and economic development in sub-Saharan Africa are under-reported
Climate adaptation in Central Asia and the Pacific islands is thinly covered
Latin America is limited to general elections and events tied to US foreign policy

events.title: Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics held
events.description: The 25th Winter Olympic Games are scheduled for 6-22 February 2026 in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy's third Winter Games after Cortina 1956 and Turin 2006. It is the first edition jointly hosted by two cities, with venues spread across Milan, Cortina, Bormio and Livorno in the northern mountains, making venue construction and transport links the main points of contention during preparation.

sources.name: International Olympic Committee announcements and Milan-Cortina 2026 organising committee material

events.certainty_note: Dates and host cities were fixed by the IOC in 2019 and published; this is a scheduled event.

events.title: FIFA World Cup held across the United States, Canada and Mexico
events.description: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is scheduled for 11 June to 19 July across sixteen host cities in the United States, Canada and Mexico — the first edition hosted by three countries and the first expanded to 48 teams. The larger format raises the group stage to 104 matches, making the North American time-zone span and cross-border travel the central scheduling problem.

sources.name: FIFA match schedule and host city announcements

events.certainty_note: Hosts, dates and the 48-team format were published by FIFA; results are outside the scope of this entry.

events.title: United States Semiquincentennial
events.description: 4 July 2026 marks 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Federal and state programmes under the Semiquincentennial banner centre on Independence Hall in Philadelphia and the National Mall. Planning has run since 2020 through the US Semiquincentennial Commission, and the commemorations have drawn open dispute over how the founding era should account for slavery and Native dispossession.

sources.name: US National Park Service and US Semiquincentennial Commission public material

events.certainty_note: The date follows directly from the year of the Declaration; programme details are published by the commission.

events.title: Brazilian general election held
events.description: Brazil holds its general election on 4 October 2026, choosing the president, vice-president, the entire Chamber of Deputies, one third of the Senate and state governors. A second round for the presidential race, if no candidate wins an absolute majority of valid votes, is scheduled for 25 October. The campaign continues the polarisation of 2022 around Amazon development, fiscal rules and the role of the judiciary.

sources.name: Brazilian Superior Electoral Court (TSE) electoral calendar

events.certainty_note: The date is set by Brazilian electoral law; candidates and results are outside the scope of this entry.

events.title: United States midterm elections held
events.description: The United States holds midterm elections on 3 November 2026, with all 435 House seats, roughly a third of the Senate and 36 governorships on the ballot. The outcome decides control of Congress in the closing stretch of Trump's second term and shapes the room available for budget, immigration and tariff policy.

sources.name: US Federal Election Commission and state election calendars

events.certainty_note: The date follows federal law (the Tuesday after the first Monday in November); results are outside the scope of this entry.

events.title: Term of the UN Secretary-General ends; succession process
events.description: The term of UN Secretary-General António Guterres ends on 31 December 2026, with the Security Council consulting on a successor from 2026 and recommending a candidate to the General Assembly. The transition again raises questions about the transparency of the selection, regional rotation and the veto power of the permanent members.

sources.name: Article 97 of the UN Charter and related General Assembly resolutions

events.certainty_note: The end of the term is a fixed fact; the successor is undetermined and no prediction is made here.
